context:
I'm a 26-year-old software developer. I've taken an indefinite break from work to strengthen/explore myself, expand my interdisciplinary knowledge graph, and venture into solo projects. My design/architectonic ethos is to be lean, rapid, and iterative, so that I can touch and explore the widest possible set of solution spaces for whatever we are pursuing. We gotta be nimble and think outside the box to eliminate the ordinary clutter/overhead as much as possible, while crafting solid and reliable artifacts. We achieve this nimbleness by leveraging high-impact architectural/systemic decisions/primitives before hitting diminishing returns, not by taking superficial trade-offs that degrade the clarity or solidity of our solutions.
A proprietary funding-rate and basis anomaly scanner for Crypto Perp-Perp arbitrage. Complements—but remains strictly decoupled from—the execution engine. Surfaces localized, pair-specific anomalies across the same 13 Asian venues the engine routes to, normalizes them into comparable units, and ranks them by deployment viability. Doubles as a longitudinal research substrate: every observation is persisted to build proprietary datasets (anomaly half-life, cross-exchange lead-lag, basis behavior during spikes, post-payout mean-reversion) that no public scanner exposes. we can edit or remove CEXs in the future. The initial 13 are: ["BINANCE", "BINGX", "BITGET", "BITMART", "BYBIT", "COINEX", "[GATE.IO", "HTX", "KUCOIN", "MEXC", "OKX", "PHEMEX", "XT.COM"]]
Public scanners (Coinglass, Zeek, Velo) are optimized for a broad retail audience and display raw per-epoch rates across heterogeneous funding intervals, which is actively misleading for viability math. This scanner encodes the operator's specific gates natively: venue-parity with the engine's routing set, epoch-normalized yield as a first-class unit, and automated Breakeven Epochs ranking. The long-term compounding asset is the historical dataset itself, not the live scanner view.
DuckDB embedded over partitioned Parquet files. Zero-daemon, columnar, analytical-SQL native, portable artifacts. Rejects Postgres (ops overhead, weak on window-heavy columnar scans), InfluxDB (schema rigidity during research phase), and SQLite (row-store, poor for analytical scans over millions of rows). Parquet partitioning: year=/month=/day=/, append-only per-cycle. A daily compaction job (idempotent, atomic per venue) consolidates each prior day's per-cycle files into one file per venue — pure storage optimization, no schema or query-semantic change.
Every observation conforms to a single locked row shape; exchange-specific idiosyncrasies never leak downstream. Fields: ts_utc (ms), exchange (canonical slug), symbol_canonical (CCXT unified, e.g., BTC/USDT:USDT), funding_rate (raw per-epoch upcoming-boundary rate; refines as TWAP-of-premium-index accumulates), funding_interval_h (positive float, hours; 1 / 4 / 8 most common), predicted_rate (forward forecast for the cycle AFTER the upcoming one — populated only where the venue publishes it), next_funding_ts (UTC-aligned settlement timestamp; mathematically derived from interval when the venue does not publish a per-symbol value), mark_price, index_price, last_price (three price columns of decreasing precision, separate primitives; downstream queries opt into precision tradeoffs explicitly), open_interest_usd, volume_24h_usd, apy_norm ($r \cdot 8760 / T_{epoch}$, computed and stored).
Every schema field has exactly one authoritative per-venue source. If the source is missing for a row, the field is NULL. No cascading fallbacks (e.g., last-trade-price substituted for mark_price, default 8h for an unknown interval) — those silently corrupt the longitudinal dataset, which is the project's compounding asset. The collector enforces the invariant at the boundary; new venues require probe-driven verification of every per-field source before integration.
REST polling at 30s cadence, one async task per venue. Per-venue strategy is bespoke — batch funding endpoints where preserved, ticker.info paths where the data is piggybacked there, per-symbol fan-out or native HTTP where neither works. WebSockets explicitly rejected for this layer: the scanner's physics is wide-and-shallow across hundreds of symbols, inverse of the engine's deep-and-narrow single-pair streams. Aggregate request budget remains comfortably under each venue's public rate limit even with concurrency-bumped fan-outs.
Scanner and engine run as fully separate OS processes with independent lifecycles and failure domains. No shared runtime state. Any engine-side read of scanner data occurs strictly via DuckDB query against Parquet files or a read-only HTTP endpoint—never via in-memory coupling. Guarantees that scanner analytics pressure can never stall the engine's event loop.
One task per exchange. Pulls the per-venue authoritative source for each schema field (documented in FIELD_NOTES.md), applies USD conversion where required, computes $APY_{norm}$, appends to the active Parquet partition. Failure of any single venue is isolated and logged; sibling collectors continue uninterrupted.
audit.py: re-probes every authoritative source per (venue, schema field) on demand against live CCXT. Run when CCXT is upgraded, when a venue's API rotates fields, or when adding a new venue. The output is the single source of truth for per-venue extraction; FIELD_NOTES.md mirrors it.
Symbols where $|APY_{norm}| \geq \theta$ AND $volume_{24h} \geq V_{min}$ AND the anomaly has persisted across $\geq N$ consecutive observations. Persistence filter rejects single-tick spikes (data errors or already-decayed transients). For every symbol listed on $\geq 2$ venues, computes $\Delta r = r_{max} - r_{min}$ and ranks. Directly maps to candidate leg-pairs for the engine. Computes $E_{BE} = (C_{basis} + C_{fees}) / Y_{epoch}$ in SQL. Taker-fee constants and basis-cost estimates are configurable per venue-pair. Candidates sort by $E_{BE}$ ascending.
Single-operator, localhost-bound. Surfaces the three analytics views as sortable tables plus per-symbol historical funding charts with cross-exchange overlay. Graduation rule: patterns earn a place on the dashboard only after proving themselves in the research layer.
Two surfaces: anomaly threshold-breach notifications driven by the analytics layer, plus a data-flow liveness watch that pings if no Parquet write is observed in a 5-minute window (cooldown to prevent spam during extended outages). Reuses the engine's Pushover credentials. Mobile surface is Pushover only; no native mobile app.
Exploratory lab bench over the same DuckDB substrate. Hosts the proprietary pattern studies: anomaly half-life distributions, cross-exchange funding lead-lag, basis behavior during anomalies, post-payout mean-reversion. Free use of sklearn/statsmodels/scipy at this layer; nothing ships to the live radar without being expressible as clear SQL logic.
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Collectors (async, one task per exchange) │ │ → normalize → append Parquet partitions │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ DuckDB (embedded, reads Parquet directly) │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ ┌──────────┐ ┌────────────┐ ┌───────────┐ │ Analytics│ │ Dashboard │ │ Research │ │ views │ │ (Plotly) │ │ notebooks │ │ │ │ │ │ │ └──────────┘ └────────────┘ └───────────┘ │ ▼ ┌──────────┐ │ Alerts │ (Pushover hook, reusing engine's creds) └──────────┘
Top-of-book snapshots only if needed. Deep L2 persistence is explicitly rejected as a storage and complexity trap. Tick-level trade ingestion out of scope. No model serving against the live radar. Statistical modeling lives in the research layer only. Single-operator, localhost-bound, mirroring the engine's deployment posture. The scanner is not a charting app, not a data platform, not a second product. Any feature pulling it in those directions is rejected.
Singapore VPS, co-located with the engine but with fully independent lifecycle. Two systemd services — arb-collector (ingestion) and arb-dashboard (Streamlit radar) — plus two cron jobs (daily Parquet compaction, 5-minute liveness watch). The engine never shares runtime state with any of them; engine-side reads of scanner data go strictly through the Parquet substrate. Shares the VPS's geographic latency barycenter across the 13 target venues, though latency is not a first-order concern for the scanner's polling cadence.
